1  (RC owner of the KSRTC Bus bearing  Reg.KA-13-F-2255)
 (By Afzal Ahmed, Adv.)

:JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner through her father against the Respondent under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 12.02.2021 at about 1.30 p.m, when the minor Petitioner was standing on the left side of the Tumkur - Bengaluru road, near 8th Mail Junction, at that time, one KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2255 driven by its driver came in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came from Tumkur side and dashed against the Petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioner had SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3211/2022 sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Prakriya Hospital, wherein minor Petitioner was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
The father of the Petitioner has spent huge amount towards medical expenses, nourishment and conveyance charges.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy.
Due to the said accident, she could not able to attend the school.
Due to the said accident, she is suffering from pain, mental agony and getting headache and lost her comfort and enjoyment of life.
The Respondent is the owner cum internal insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, it is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondent, Respondent has appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement inter-alia denied the age of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries SCCH 15 4 MVC No.3211/2022 sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.

Further it contended that the offending KSRTC bus was proceeding on schedule route from Arkalgud to Bengaluru at about 1.30 p.m., when the said bus was proceeding on National Highway, near 8 th Mile, there was traffic signal and the driver had stopped the bus and waiting for green signal and after green signal the driver has moved the bus slowly, at that time the Petitioner along with her mother and aunty who got down from another bus, suddenly came running near the front left side of the bus and

by seeing this, the driver who most cautious applied brakes suddenly and stopped the bus, in spite of Chethana.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107510392/
2 which the Petitioner came in contact with the left side corner and fell down and had sustained minor injuries.
Further, it contended that on humanitarian ground, it has paid a sum of Rs.5,000/- to the father of the Petitioner for immediate medical expenses.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, Respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

6. On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3211/2022 following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 12.10.2019 at about 1.30 p.m., on NH-4, Tumkur - Bengaluru road, near 8th Mile Junction, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2255?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case of the minor Petitioner, the guardian/father of the minor Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents at Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-11.
Further, he examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 5 documents at Ex.P12 to Ex.P.16 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand, the Respondent has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked one SCCH 15 6 MVC No.3211/2022 document at Ex.R1 and closed its side evidence.
8.

Having heard the arguments by the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order, for the following:

REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2255 by its driver.
10.
On the other hand, the Respondent had denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.

Chethana.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107510392/
3 11.
In order to prove the case of the minor Petitioner, the natural guardian of the minor Petitioner i.e., her father SCCH 15 7 MVC No.3211/2022 by name Sri.
Narayana
S / o Ramakrishnappa
got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
PW.1 has also examined two witnesses by name Sujatha as P.W.2 and Dr. Nagaraj B.N as PW.3 and got marked 5 documents at Ex.P-12 to Ex.P-16.
P.W.1 has re- iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.
Ex.P-1 to 11 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar with Sketch, IMV report, Wound Certificate, Charge-sheet, Medical bills, Advance receipts, Discharge summary and Aadhaar cards.

12. Upon going through Ex.P-1 and Ex.P-2 i.e., FIR and Complaint shows that the Complaint was lodged by the father of the minor Petitioner before Peenya Traffic Police Station and the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2255 for the offences punishable under sec. 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P-3 is the Spot panchanama with Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P-4 is the IMV report which shows that the SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3211/2022 accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P5 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injury.

Ex.P-6 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Peenya Traffic Police Station has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending KSRTC bus for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.
13. Ex.P7 is the Medical bills.
Ex.P8 is the Advance Receipts.
Ex. P9
is the Discharge summary.
Ex.P10 & 11 are the Aadhaar cards.
14. Further, P.W.1 has examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.3 and he also re-iterated about the injuries sustained by the minor Petitioner in a RTA.
PW.1 is subjected for cross- examination by the Learned Counsel for Respondent.
But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.

To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent has examined its bus conductor by name N.S.
Premkumar as RW.1 and got marked Authorization letter at Ex.R1 and SCCH 15 9 MVC No.3211/2022 nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the PW.1.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that PW.1 has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2255 by its driver and in the said accident, the minor Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No. 2:

As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending KSRTC bus by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16.
As per the Ex.P5 Wound Certificate, the Petitioner sustained degloving injury of right leg and foot.
In this regard, next friend of the Petitioner i.e., his father deposed as PW-1.
As per the Wound Certificate, the Petitioner has taken treatment at Prakriya hospital, Bengaluru.
As per the opinion of the doctor, the said injury is grievous in nature.

The SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3211/2022 Petitioner also produced Discharge summary of Prakriya hospital at Ex-P9 and the same goes to show that the Petitioner was admitted in the said hospital from 12.10.2019 to 24.10.2019.
Chethana.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107510392/
4 17.
The Petitioner has examined doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as PW-3 and he assessed the disability of minor Petitioner at 12% towards whole body.
The age of the Petitioner is 4 years and 11 months and 6 days.
As such question of occupation and income does not arise.

In the circumstances,
any disability shown to her limb cannot be assessed as functional disability.
18. According to the evidence of doctor/PW-3, the minor Petitioner has suffered physical disability at 12% to the whole body.
PW.3 in his cross-examination deposed that he has not personally treated the Petitioner.
Further he admitted that the minor Petitioner does not sustained fracture and he did not get the opinion of the treated doctor of the Petitioner at the time of assessed disability.
It is worth to note here that PW.1 in his cross-examination admitted SCCH 15 11 MVC No.3211/2022 that now his daughter i.e., minor Petitioner is going to school.
Hence, it is proper to take the physical disability of the minor Petitioner at 10% towards whole body.

In view of a decision passed in Civil Appeal No.7139/2013 (Master Mallikarjun Vs Division Manager, National Insurance Co., Ltd., and another) by the Hon'ble Apex Court, if the disability is up to 10% of the whole body, the minor Petitioner would be entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendance etc., towards conventional heads like pain and sufferings already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship inconvenience,
discomforts etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.
19.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.7139/2013 (Master Mallikarjun Vs Division Manager, National Insurance Co., Ltd., and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In addition to the compensation towards conventional heads, the minor Petitioner is also entitled for compensation under the heads like discomfort and inconvenience to the parents and their loss of earnings during the period of hospitalization of the Petitioner and towards medical expenditure.
With regard to the case on hand, it is established that the Petitioner was hospitalized for SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3211/2022 a period of 13 days.
During the said period, since the Petitioner is minor and just at the age of 5 years, her parents might have attended her.
As such, her parents lost their earnings during that period.
In the absence of proof of income of her parents, it would be lawful to award Rs.10,000/- as compensation towards loss of earnings and their discomfort.
20. With regard to medical expenditure, hospital bills are produced at Ex-P7 totally amounting to Rs.1,37,389/-.

Since the genuineness of these documents has not been disproved on the part of the Respondent, it is established that the Petitioner has incurred medical expenditure of Rs.1,37,389/-
and by rounding off the same, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,37,400/- by way of compensation.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
 21.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3211/2022 1.

Pain, shock & Suffering, Rs.1,00,000/-
Chethana.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107510392/

5 loss of amenities 2. Loss of income of the Rs. 10,000/-
parents during the laid up period 3.

Medical expenditure Rs.1,37,400/-
 Total Rs.2,47,400/-
 22.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.2,47,400/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

23. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2255.
It is contention of the Respondent that, it has paid a sum of Rs.5,000/- as ex-gratia payment to the father of the Petitioner.

At this juncture, I would like to rely on the Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.103515 of SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3211/2022 2016 (MV-I) dated 20.06.2024 between The Managing Director, KSRTC North West Division Vs. Shivanandappa, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to observed that "Ex-gratia amount is different from the compensation awarded under the MV Act.

entities.text: MFA No.103515 of SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3211/2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: KSRTC North West Division Vs. Shivanandappa,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex-gratia payment is voluntary, whereas the compensation awarded under the M.V. Act is mandatory on the basis of liability or contractual liability.
Hence, we do not see merit in any contentions of the Learned Counsel for the NWKRTC that Ex-gratia is received by the claimants and hence they are not entitled for compensation.
The said contention is hereby rejected."

24. By relying on the said observations made by our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above stated Judgment, in the present case also, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the payment made by the Respondent i.e., Rs.5,000/- as Ex-gratia cannot be deducted from the total compensation awarded to the Petitioner.
In this case, the Respondent is the R.C. Owner cum Internal Insurer of KSRTC bus.
Therefore, the Respondent has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3211/2022 answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
25. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2 , I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
Chethana.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107510392/
6 The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.2,47,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent being the owner cum internal Insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being the deposit of the award amount and interest by the Respondent, out of the amount awarded to the minor SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3211/2022 Petitioner, Rs.1,37,400/- shall be released in favour of the father of the minor Petitioner, as a medical expenses borne by him, by way of E-Payment after his proper identification and remaining award amount shall be kept in FD in the name of the minor Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank till she attains the age of majority.
Further, the natural guardian/father of the minor Petitioner is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioner.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on the computer, print out taken by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the open Court on this the 7th day of October, 2024)
(Smt. Kumari Sujatha.)
